documented_probe: diagnose-and-repair of a seeded race condition in a concurrent asyncio service. The agent must identify the non-atomic read-modify-write across the simulated slow I/O await in the shipped word-count service (naming the exact read/await/write lines of the pristine original in /app/diagnosis.md), repair the merge into a synchronous critical section in /app/svc/wordcount_service.py, and demonstrate that the documented 40-worker load then matches the sequential ground truth. The verifier independently recomputes expected counts from the deterministic schedule rule (seeded randrange draws, round-robin workers), runs the pristine load generator unmodified, re-runs the pristine original service under the same load and requires it to still corrupt, hash-checks the fixtures, and probes 3 hidden corpus/load configs with different worker counts (24x9, 60x5, 12x25) including blank-line, huge-token, mixed-case and whitespace-padded documents.
notes: Medium: the race is invisible under a sequential run (workers=1 is exact even with the bug), so the agent must reason about cooperative asyncio scheduling to explain why 40 concurrent workers lose increments. Nonzero debugging_ambiguity (bug only manifests under load; exact lost value is nondeterministic), reasoning_depth (interleaving analysis, fix classes: atomic sync merge vs asyncio.Lock), hidden_case_generalization (hidden corpora+worker counts recomputed independently, so hardcoding fails), quantitative_correctness (exact integer equality on every hidden case), resource_pressure (40+ concurrent workers through loopback), interaction_statefulness (shared dict accumulates across many requests), dependent_stages (diagnose -> repair -> verify under documented and hidden loads).
